QUOTE: "The 16-bit layout (documented in `include/mbedtls/error.h:17-60`) splits the code into a 3-bit high-level module (mask `0xFF80`) and a 7-bit low-level module. That is why one return value can carry two names." and "join as "high : low" into buf (or whichever part exists"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that a code has a high-level module part and a low-level part, and that mbedtls_strerror renders both joined as "high : low" when both are present.
